paper_title: CAPSTONE Curriculum Sampling for Dense Retrieval with Document   Expansion
caption: Results of DPR with corpus, document, and asymmetric expansion on the dev set of MS-Marco.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of different variants of the DPR (Dense Passage Retriever) model on the MS-Marco dev set, measured by MRR@10, as a function of the number of queries used during inference. The x-axis, labeled "Number of queries used during inference (S)", ranges from 2 to 10 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 2. The y-axis, labeled "MRR@10", ranges from 33.0 to 36.0 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.5. The plot displays four distinct lines: a black solid line for "DPR w/o query", a red solid line with circular markers for "DPR w/ corpus expansion", a green solid line with triangular markers for "DPR w/ document expansion", and a blue solid line with star markers for "DPR w/ asymmetric expansion". The "DPR w/o query" line remains flat at a value of approximately 34.2. The "DPR w/ corpus expansion" line starts at approximately 35.2, increases to a peak of about 35.7 at 6 queries, and then slightly decreases to around 35.6 at 10 queries. The "DPR w/ document expansion" line starts at about 34.6, rises to a peak of roughly 35.0 at 2 queries, and then gradually declines to about 34.5 at 10 queries. The "DPR w/ asymmetric expansion" line begins at approximately 34.6, increases to a peak of about 35.0 at 2 queries, and then steadily decreases to around 34.4 at 10 queries.
